mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 2.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained UNRATE > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both decline > 1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative when both INDPRO and HOUST fall by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate below 1% during a recession signals a policy-driven monetary easing, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS < 1% and UNRATE > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and retail sales (RSAFS) by more than 0.5% month-over-month signals robust demand growth, which boosts corporate earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and RSAFS both rise > 0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when both GDPC1 and RSAFS increase by more than 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months signals labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by > 100,000 jobs per month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of monthly PAYEMS declines exceeding 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous acceleration in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a supply-side recovery, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days, except during periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%).
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 1% MoM AND CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 1% MoM and CPIAUCSL YoY <= 4%, or if returns are positive but CPIAUCSL YoY > 4%.
